findings.title: Raw-count scan is not scoped to the product's shape, so coverage will false-flag once a second product exists
findings.description: `raw_counts` counts every `tick_trade` row in the session time windows, for all instruments. `ledger_totals` is filtered by the product's shape (dataset, symbols, stype_in, tier units). `build_coverage` runs once per universe entry and compares the two in `_session_row`. Any instrument that belongs to another product, or is not covered by this shape, appears with ledger 0 and raw N. That is reported as a mismatch and exits 3. `TICK_UNIVERSE` currently holds only `ES` (`universe.py:45`), so nothing fails today. Adding a second product would make `coverage` fail for every product with overlapping sessions. Scope the raw scan to the shape's instruments, for example by joining the ledger's instrument ids. Alternatively, assert and document the single-product assumption at the call site.

findings.title: `caught_up` reports "yes" vacuously when a tier is configured but the wanted range is unknown
findings.description: `wanted` is `None` when the edge has never been observed and the entry has no `end`. `caught_up` is still called with `wanted=wanted_start is not None`. In that case the verdicts cover only sessions that already hold units, and an empty or all-complete list makes `caught_up` return `True` (`tick_status.py:159`). The render then prints "caught up: yes", though nothing established what was wanted. The project rule says to fail explicitly rather than use silent fallbacks. Pass `wanted=wanted is not None`, so this case reports `n/a`. A separate "range unknown" state would be better if the distinction matters. The CLI tests don't cover this combination, so add a case for it.

findings.title: Duplicate `shape_units` query per product in status
findings.description: `_scope` calls `shape_units` to find the held days. `session_verdicts` then calls it again for the same shape. That is two identical manifest scans per product on each `status` run. Fetch the units once and pass them to both. This would also remove the chance of the two reads seeing different snapshots.

findings.title: Module-level `assert` guards the bucket layout
findings.description: The check that `_BUCKET_ROWS` covers every `TickSessionStatus` is a bare `assert`. It is stripped under `python -O`, and an import-time `AssertionError` is a poor failure mode for a CLI. A unit test asserting the same set equality would give the same protection without the runtime hazard.

findings.title: Small cleanups
findings.description:
- `_read_storage` is a function whose only job is to defer an import. `run_mapped` could take the exception class directly, or `TickDatabaseUnreachable` could map to storage in `exit_code_for` with the writers keeping their preflight behavior another way.
- `tick_status_render.py` has no direct unit test. `age`, `_product_lines` and the no-contracts and edge-never-observed branches are exercised only through integration CLI output. A few parametrized unit tests would be cheap.
- `edge_age_seconds` can be negative if `observed_at` is in the future, and `age()` would then render a nonsense "0m". This is unlikely, but worth clamping or flagging.

findings.title: Safety, SQL, exception handling and refactors
findings.description:
- All SQL is parameterized. The only f-strings interpolate module-level `LiteralString` constants.
- `run_mapped` keeps its documented process-boundary `except Exception` and re-raises unmapped exceptions.
- `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, so the writers' behavior is unchanged while `status` and `coverage` get exit 4.
- The `utc_midnight` and `days_touched` extraction removes duplicated logic without changing behavior.
- The DELETE statements in the tests target throwaway fixture databases, and no test reads a production URL variable.
